text:
ellie (design): dropped a prototype for the new "create-connector" form. biggest open items: when to show validation (onChange vs onBlur vs onSubmit), required-field signals in compact forms, and delete-confirm behavior for connectors with downstream bindings. link: https://www.figma.com/file/efgh5678/connectors-form raphael (eng): onChange gives faster feedback but noisy for slow validators (server-side). can do optimistic client checks onChange and server validation onSubmit; debounce network calls. morgan (product): important: during onboarding we want fewer blockers so maybe show gentle inline hints onChange but only hard error onSubmit. For power users we can surface stricter inline errors. lee (a11y): accessibility: any live validation must be exposed via aria-live. prefer `aria-live="polite"` for non-blocking hints and `assertive` for blocking errors. also ensure `aria-describedby` ties input to the message. ellie (design): good — plan: 1) client-side format checks onChange (polite), 2) server-side authoritative errors onSubmit (assertive). we'll mark the message container with role=alert for the assertive case. example per input: ```html
Friendly hint about allowed chars
Names can only contain letters, numbers, and -
``` raphael (eng): looks fine. tiny perf note: avoid adding/removing nodes in DOM order causing focus shifts. hide/show with `visibility` or `height` transitions. morgan (product): required marker debate: asterisk vs label vs required on placeholder. On mobile we have limited horizontal space; placeholders disappear on focus. prefer a persistent tiny label or an inline suffix "(required)". lee (a11y): do not rely on placeholder for required info. screen readers won't announce placeholder reliably and it vanishes on focus. `aria-required="true"` on the input plus visible label is best. ellie (design): I'll test two patterns in Figma: compact suffix `(req)` vs full `Required` under the field. Compact is for dense tables/forms. raphael (eng): implementation idea: expose a form-level setting `requiredDisplay: 'suffix'|'inline'|false` so we can switch without changing markup per field. morgan (product): delete behavior: connectors can have downstream jobs. typed-confirm is heavy. options: (A) single modal + list of affected resources + undo toast, (B) typed-confirm for more than N dependents, (C) soft-delete to trash with restore. need a policy recommendation. ellie (design): mock for A and B. copy consideration: show count and sample names instead of raw list where long. e.g., "Deleting 42 jobs that reference this connector: sample-job-1, sample-job-2..." lee (a11y): if we list affected resources, ensure the modal is keyboard-scrollable and focus-trap includes the list. For typed-confirm, offer an alternative like a checkbox "I understand this will delete X resources" because retyping can be a barrier. raphael (eng): backend note: soft-delete needs retention policy. undo toast can rely on soft-delete too. typed-confirm requires verifying input against a stable identifier (not just display name) to prevent spoofing. morgan (product): I'm leaning to: undo toast for <=10 items, checkbox + modal for 11-100, typed-confirm for >100 or org-wide. we should A/B test thresholds. ellie (design): microcopy recs for modal header: prefer explicit subject-first copy: "Delete connector 'stripe-payments' and 8 dependent jobs" then body: "This cannot be undone. You can restore items from Trash within 30 days." Primary button: "Delete connector" (destructive). avoid vague "Are you sure?" raphael (eng): one more: error tone. let's keep helpful suggestions: e.g., "Name already taken" -> "That name's in use — try adding a suffix like -2". short actionable text reduces support tickets. lee (a11y): color contrast and icons: never rely on color alone. show an error icon + text and ensure 3:1 contrast at minimum for non-text UI components. Test with VoiceOver and NVDA. devops-bot: design-lint: token-contrast-check passed for connector-form tokens, but `--error-red-300` flagged as borderline; manual review recommended. ellie (design): thanks — action items: update Figma with onChange polite vs onSubmit assertive flows, add compact suffix mock, create modal variants A/B, and draft microcopy list (5 examples). will loop the eng/a11y folks for review. morgan (product): please also add a one-pager A/B plan with metrics: accidental-delete rate, restore rate, form completion time. thanks!
